sections.h2: Where is Charleston County, SC, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Charleston County runs along the Atlantic coast in the Lowcountry and is the largest county in South Carolina by total land and water area, at 1,357.99 square miles. Water makes up 440.01 of those miles, about 32.4 percent, and the county borders Berkeley, Georgetown, Colleton and Dorchester counties.

The county was chartered in 1785, dissolved soon after over disputes about its governance, and redrawn in 1798, with the boundaries taking effect on January 1, 1800. It is named for King Charles II, and the city of Charleston is the county seat.

Island and coastal communities include Isle of Palms, Folly Beach, Kiawah Island, Seabrook Island and Sullivan's Island. Which municipality a house sits in changes the tax bill, since cities and towns set their own rates on top of the county's.

sections.h2: How many people live in Charleston County, and where?
sections.html:
The 2020 Census counted 408,235 people, up 16.6 percent from 350,209 in 2010, and a 2025 estimate is 436,200. About 90.9 percent of residents live in urban areas, and the median age is 38.3.

sections.h2: What does the Charleston County economy look like?
sections.html:
The county's 2022 gross domestic product was $41 billion, and total employment was 275,580 with an average annual wage of $62,132. Unemployment ranged between 2 percent and 3.3 percent from 2022 through 2024.

  • Health care and social assistance: 43,511 jobs, or 15.8 percent.
  • Accommodation and food services: 36,926 jobs, or 13.4 percent.
  • Retail trade: 29,556 jobs, or 10.7 percent.
  • Professional, scientific and technical services: 21,576 jobs, or 7.8 percent.
  • Educational services: 19,571 jobs, or 7.1 percent.

Named top employers include Boeing, Booz Allen Hamilton, the Charleston County School District, the College of Charleston, the Medical University of South Carolina, Mercedes-Benz Group, the U.S. Department of Defense and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Tourism sites such as Fort Sumter, Boone Hall and Magnolia Plantation also draw visitors to the county.

sections.h2: Which Charleston County office collects property tax?
sections.html:
The Charleston County Treasurer collects real estate tax at the O.T. Wallace County Office Building, 101 Meeting Street, Suite 120, Charleston 29401. The phone is (843) 958-4360, and the hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Mail checks or money orders payable to the Charleston County Treasurer to P.O. Box 878, Charleston, SC 29402-0878. Online payment is available through the county's public access site, and a surcharge applies to card payments. The Treasurer does not accept partial payments under state law.

The Treasurer does not keep property or owner addresses. Address changes go to the Assessor and the Auditor, which is worth remembering after a sale if bills are still going to the old owner.

sections.h2: When are Charleston County property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due January 15 of the following year, and the penalty is 3 percent after that date, 10 percent in total after February 1, and 15 percent in total after March 17. After March 17 the bill goes to the Delinquent Tax Department.

The Treasurer also runs an advance installment plan for real property owners whose accounts are not escrowed by a mortgage company and who owe nothing from earlier years. It costs nothing extra and has six payments: five equal advance payments on the 15th of February, April, June, August and October, then a balance mailed by November 15 and due by January 15.

Receipts are mailed to the address on the tax bill, or to a new address if you send a change-of-address form with the payment. Online payers get an on-screen confirmation and an email.

sections.h2: What happened in the 2025 Charleston County reassessment?
sections.html:
Charleston County ran a countywide reassessment in 2025, with notices mailed in August 2025 and an appeal deadline of November 18, 2025, according to the City of Isle of Palms. The city also reports most properties were protected by a 15 percent cap on taxable value increases, but properties sold or transferred in 2024, newly added or substantially improved may not be.

State law then requires cities to adjust their rates to stay revenue neutral, based on a rollback figure the Auditor calculates. The reassessment hotline is (843) 958-4144.

Three levels of review exist: an objection is an informal review, a protest is a formal review, and an appeal goes to the Board of Assessment Appeals. After the board, state law gives 30 days to ask for a hearing at the Administrative Law Court. State law sets reassessment on a five-year cycle, so ask the Assessor when the next one is scheduled.

sections.h2: Which exemptions matter when you sell or buy in Charleston County?
sections.html:
Charleston County offers a 4 percent legal residence rate, a homestead exemption, and an ATI exemption, each with its own deadline. The county's tax exemptions page says the 4 percent application deadline is typically January 15 each year, and applications are available as a PDF or online.

  • Homestead: excludes the first $50,000 of the fair market value of a legal residence for owners who meet age, disability or blindness rules, have lived in South Carolina for a year, and hold title by December 31 of the prior year.
  • ATI exemption: partly exempts up to 25 percent of the value that results from an assessable transfer, if the property was taxed at 6 percent before and after, rose in value because of the transfer, and was on the roll in the year of sale.
  • ATI deadline: on or before January 30 of the tax year requested.

Contact the Homestead Representative at (843) 958-4220 for the first, and the Assessor for the rest. Under state law, a sale is an assessable transfer that resets the value for the next owner, with listed exclusions for some family and affiliated transfers.

sections.h2: Selling a Charleston County house with tax owed
sections.html:
If taxes are unpaid at closing, the closing agent pays them from your sale proceeds, and you avoid the 15 percent total penalty and the risk of a delinquent sale. After a delinquent tax sale, the owner or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within twelve months by paying taxes, penalties and costs plus interest that rises from 3 percent to 12 percent over the year.

faqs.q: When are Charleston County, SC property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 15 of the following year. The penalty is 3 percent after January 15, 10 percent in total after February 1, and 15 percent in total after March 17.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Charleston County property tax?
faqs.a: The Treasurer is at 101 Meeting Street, Suite 120, Charleston, and takes mail payments at P.O. Box 878, Charleston, SC 29402-0878. You can also pay online, and the phone is (843) 958-4360.

faqs.q: Can I pay Charleston County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Treasurer's advance installment plan, if the account is not escrowed and has no outstanding taxes. It has five advance payments and a final balance due by January 15.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to apply for the 4 percent rate in Charleston County?
faqs.a: The county says it is typically January 15 each year. Applications are available as a PDF or online.

faqs.q: How much is the Charleston County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It excludes the first $50,000 of fair market value of a legal residence for owners who meet the age, disability or blindness rules and the residency and title requirements.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Charleston County house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent can pay the taxes and penalties out of your proceeds. A tax sale can still be redeemed within twelve months if one has already occurred.
